info.title: Synapse Public API
info.description:
The Synapse public API, for partners and a venue's own developers.

**Auth.** `Authorization: Bearer syn_live_…` — an API key created in Settings → API keys.
Each key carries scopes; a call without the scope it needs is 403 `insufficient_scope`.
Installed apps send `Authorization: Bearer syn_at_…`, an OAuth access token from `/oauth/token`.
The venue approves each app's scopes, and a token lasts an hour before it is renewed with a refresh token.

**Errors** are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`. Branch on `code`, never on `detail`.

**Lists** are cursor-paginated: `limit` (≤200) and `cursor`, answered with
`{ data, has_more, next_cursor }`. Syncable lists take `updated_since`.

**Idempotency.** Creates and money-moving calls take an `Idempotency-Key` header; a retry
with the same key and body returns the original response with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`.

**Rate limits.** 50-request burst, 1,000 an hour per key. See the `RateLimit-*` headers;
a 429 carries `Retry-After`.

**Money** is `{ minor, currency }`. Instants are RFC 3339 UTC.

apiKey.description: An API key (syn_live_…) or an installed app's OAuth access token (syn_at_…).

scopes.members:sensitive: See allergies, access needs and case detail
scopes.reservations:write: Create, change, seat and cancel reservations
scopes.tickets:write: Issue, check in and cancel tickets
scopes.checkins:write: Check people in and issue guest passes
scopes.loyalty:write: Top up and adjust loyalty balances

get.description: Returns the key or installed app that made the call: its ID, organisation, scopes, the venues it is limited to (empty means all) and whether it is a live or test key. For an installed app, installation_id and application_id (the app's client ID) are set; for a key both are null. Any valid key or installation can call it, whatever its scopes, so use it to check the credential works.

delete.description: An installed app removes its own installation: its access and refresh tokens stop working, and its webhook endpoints are disabled. The organisation keeps its record of the install. Only an installed app's access token can make this call; an API key gets a 400.

get.description: The organisation's venues this key may use, with each one's IANA time zone (dates such as arrival_date are in it).

Every member of the organisation, oldest first by `created_at`, or by `updated_at` with `updated_since`, for syncing. Merged members are included (`status: merged`, `merged_into`) so a sync can follow them. `email` matches exactly, ignoring case. A key limited to venues still sees every member.

post.description: Adds a member, as staff do from the directory: the member's contact record is matched or created and `member.created` is emitted. `status` defaults to `active` and cannot be `merged`. `sensitive` needs a key holding `members:sensitive`.

get.summary: Get a member by your own id
get.description: The member you linked to `ref` under `source` (for example your CRM's id for the person). The pair is yours alone: another organisation using the same pair reaches its own member.

put.summary: Create or update a member by your own id
put.description: Creates the member and links it to `ref` under `source`, or updates the one already linked, in one transaction. The pair is yours alone: another organisation using the same pair gets a member of its own. 201 when created, 200 when updated; fields left out of an update stay as they are. A merged member is refused (409 `member_merged`), and so is a member erased at their request (409 `conflict`).

get.description: One member. A merged member answers too, with `status: merged` and `merged_into` naming the member that took its place.

patch.description: Changes the fields you send; the rest stay. `null` clears an optional field. A change emits `member.updated`, and a new `status` also `member.status_changed`; sending what is already there changes and emits nothing. A merged member is refused (409 `member_merged`), and `status` cannot be set to `merged`.

post.description: Folds the member in `from` into the member in the path, in one transaction. The member in the path keeps its own details, takes the stricter of the two door flags and adds the other's recorded access and health notes, and gains the other's check-ins, reservations, bookings, tickets, guest passes, guests, cases, checks and cloakroom tickets. The other's contact, guest record and external refs move only when this member has none of its own (external refs per `source`). Each loyalty balance moves as a pair of adjustments, so totals are unchanged. The other's membership and day passes are revoked; its booking tickets follow their bookings and show the member that stays. The other member then answers GETs with `status: "merged"` and `merged_into`, and can no longer be changed or signed in to the member portal. Refused with 409 `merge_conflict` for a member merged into itself or one already merged, and with 409 `merge_blocked` (listing `blockers`) while the other member has live billing: a subscription, an unpaid invoice, an account balance, a direct debit, a scheduled first payment or a saved card. Returns the member that stays.

get.description: Check-ins (`checkins:read`), table and room reservations (`reservations:read`, a table needs the bookings module and a room the rooms module) and event tickets (`tickets:read`) for one member, newest first; POS checks too when the POS product is on and the key has `checks:read`, loyalty ledger entries with `loyalty:read`, and cases with `cases:read`. Each item has a `type`, the instant it `occurred_at`, the item's own public `id` and a short plain-English `summary`. A key limited to venues sees only check-ins, reservations, tickets and checks at those venues, and only loyalty entries tied to a check at one of them; cases are never venue-limited. Page with `limit` and `cursor`; the cursor is opaque.

Applications under review or decided, oldest first by `created_at` — or by `updated_at` with `updated_since`, for syncing. Drafts are never listed. A key limited to venues sees only applicants of those venues.

post.description: Starts an application at status `new`, as staff do when they enter one by hand. A key limited to venues must give a `venue_id` it covers.

get.summary: Get an applicant by your own id
get.description: The applicant you linked to `ref` under `source` (for example your CRM's id for the lead).

put.summary: Create or update an applicant by your own id
put.description: Creates the applicant and links it to `ref` under `source`, or updates the one already linked. The pair is yours alone: another organisation using the same pair gets its own applicant. 201 when created, 200 when updated; fields left out of an update stay as they are. A converted applicant is refused (409 `applicant_converted`).

patch.description: Changes the fields you send; the rest stay. `null` clears a field. A converted applicant is refused (409 `applicant_converted`). Moving along the review pipeline is a decision, not an update.

post.summary: Move an applicant along the review pipeline
post.description: Moves the application to `rating`, `pipeline`, `approved`, `rejected` or `frozen`: only the moves staff can make, each recorded against the key. Approving while some proposers have not confirmed answers 409 `proposers_unconfirmed` with `proposers`; send `override_proposers: true` to approve anyway. An illegal move is 409 `invalid_transition`. Rejecting with `email_applicant: true` sends the club's rejection email.

post.summary: Convert an approved applicant into a member
post.description: Creates the member from an `approved` applicant. With `plan_id`, the first membership payment is quoted and scheduled after the usual notice (the key must cover every venue); `waive_joining_fee` waives the plan's joining fee. Anything but an approved applicant is 409 `invalid_transition`; one already converted is 409 `applicant_converted`.

get.description: Events (functions), oldest first by `created_at`, or by `updated_at` with `updated_since`, for syncing. Filter by venue, category, status, or a start time from `from` up to (not including) `to`. A key limited to venues sees only events at one of them, never an org-wide one.

post.description: Creates a draft event at a venue, with one General admission tier at `price` (free when left out). Without `venue_id` the event is org-wide, which only a key covering every venue may create. PATCH `status` to `published` to put it on sale to members.

get.description: One event with its category and the ticket tiers on sale to the public: each tier's price, places left (counting the event's capacity) and sales window. Hidden tiers (bought with a code, or a guest list's) are not listed.

patch.description: Changes only the fields sent; null clears an optional one. A new start time or `cancelled` tells the ticket holders, as a change by staff does. An event stays at its venue, and its prices live on its tiers.

get.description: The club's own kinds of event, archived ones included (`archived`: kept on their events, not given to new ones). Read-only.
The event's tickets, oldest first by `created_at`, or by `updated_at` with `updated_since`. Filter by status.

post.description: Takes `quantity` places from a tier (the event's first public one when `tier_id` is left out) for a member or a named guest. A hidden tier is bought by its id with the `unlock_code` the club gave out; without it, or with a wrong one, or for a guest list's own tier, the answer is 404 `not_found` (tier), so a hidden tier never shows. The member must be active (400 otherwise). A member's ticket is charged to their card on file, as a staff sale is; with no card, or for a guest, it stays `reserved` until paid at the door. The tier's window, audience and limits apply. No places left, in the event, the tier or its list, or a closed sales window: 409 `sold_out`, and nothing is reserved.

Checks in every place on the ticket not yet in, at the event's venue (name it in `venue_id` for an org-wide event). The door's rules hold and only door staff can override them: the occupancy limit reached, someone flagged not to be admitted, or a cancelled ticket is 409 `admission_refused`, and nothing is checked in. Everyone already in: 409 `already_checked_in`.

An unpaid ticket is admitted too: a guest's ticket, or a member's with no card, is paid at the door. Check `amount_due` first, and collect it at the door; `paid` stays false until the club records the payment.
Cancels the ticket and gives its places back. Nothing is refunded: a refund is the club's to make. Cancelling a cancelled ticket answers it as it is.

get.description: Check-ins of every kind (members, guests, event tickets), oldest first by `created_at`. `since` keeps those from that instant on; `venue_id` and `member_id` narrow the list. A key limited to venues sees only its venues' check-ins; one with no venue is visible to org-wide keys only.

post.description: Checks a member in at a venue, with method `manual`. A merged member's id checks in whoever they were merged into. A member flagged to watch or not to admit is checked in and the venue's managers are alerted, as at the door. Event tickets are checked in with `POST /tickets/{id}/checkin`.

get.description: Guest passes, oldest first by `created_at`, or by `updated_at` with `updated_since`. Filter by the night (`valid_on`), the host member, the type and the status. A key limited to venues sees its venues' passes and those valid at any venue.

post.description: Issues a `day` pass (a non-member, by `holder_name`) or a `guest` pass for a member's guest (`host_member_id` and `guest_name`), valid on `valid_on` (the venue's calendar date, today by default). A merged host member hosts through whoever they were merged into. With `guest_email` or `guest_phone` the guest is matched or made as a person and the pass is their visit under the host's guest number; adding the same guest for the same night again returns the same pass. A pass with `venue_id` is valid only at that venue; a key limited to one venue issues for it, one limited to several must name one, and an org-wide key may leave it out for a pass valid anywhere. Nothing is sent to the guest.

get.description: The organisation's cloakroom tickets, oldest first by `created_at`, or by `updated_at` with `updated_since`. Filter by `status` or `member_id`. A key limited to venues sees only its venues' tickets.

post.description: Stores items for a member (`member_id`) or a named guest (`holder_name`) at a venue (`venue_id`, which may be left out when the key or the organisation has one venue) and returns the ticket with its claim `code`. A member who was merged away is stored against the member they were folded into.

post.summary: Hand items back by claim code
post.description: Marks the ticket with this `code` collected and emits `cloakroom.collected`. An unknown code is a 404; a ticket already handed back is a 409 `already_collected`.
Marks the ticket collected and emits `cloakroom.collected`. A ticket already handed back is a 409 `already_collected`.

get.description: The organisation's loyalty programmes, oldest first by `created_at`, or by `updated_at` with `updated_since`. `monthly_credit` is what each renewal credits: `reset` tops the balance up to it, `accumulate` adds it.

Members' memberships of the organisation's programmes, with their balances, oldest first by `joined_at`. `member_id` and `program_id` narrow the list. A key limited to venues still sees every membership.

post.summary: Enrol a member in a programme
post.description: Enrols a member in a loyalty programme with a zero balance. A member holds one membership per programme: when they already have it, it comes back unchanged with 200 (201 when it is new). A merged member's id enrols whoever they were merged into.

get.description: One membership, with its balance.

Every movement of the balance, oldest first by `created_at`: renewals, top-ups, redemptions, reversals of refunded redemptions, and adjustments. `amount` is signed and `balance_after` is the balance the entry left. A key limited to venues sees only entries tied to a check at one of its venues; the rest name no venue.

post.description: Credits the balance with money the partner has taken: no payment is recorded here. `amount.currency` must be the organisation's. Emits `loyalty.credited`. Org-wide keys only: a top-up names no venue, so a key limited to venues gets 403.

get.description: Members' own wallet passes (`membership`, `loyalty` and `day_pass`), oldest first by `created_at`. Filter by `member_id`, `status` and `type`. Guests' passes, event tickets and booking tickets (a table booking or a room stay) are not listed here. A pass never exposes its serial, barcode or device details.

post.description: Issues (or re-issues, reactivating a revoked one) a member's pass for a wallet platform. `type` is `membership` (the default), `loyalty` or `day_pass`; the others belong to a booking, a guest or an event ticket. A merged member's id issues the survivor's pass. The answer carries `install_url`, a link you send the member to add the pass to their wallet; it is shown here only. `pass.issued` is emitted.

get.description: The member's own passes (`membership`, `loyalty` and `day_pass`; not their booking tickets), oldest first by `created_at`, as `GET /passes` with the member fixed. A merged member's passes were revoked at the merge; list the survivor's for the live ones.

post.summary: Issue a member a wallet pass
post.description: As `POST /passes`, for the member in the path.

Revokes a member's own pass (`membership`, `loyalty` or `day_pass`; any other pass is a 404): it stops admitting and the holder's wallet is told to show it void. Any `install_url` sent for that member and pass type stops working, on either platform, so the pass can't be added again from it; issue it again to send a new one. Revoking a revoked pass changes nothing and emits nothing. `pass.revoked` is emitted.

get.description: The organisation's membership plans, cheapest first (deleted plans are not listed). Prices are per `interval`, VAT included, in the plan's own currency; `vat_rate_pct` is a percentage (20 = 20 %). `subscriber_count` counts every subscription ever taken on the plan. There is one page: `has_more` is always false.

Members' subscriptions, oldest first by `created_at`, or by `updated_at` with `updated_since`. Filter by member and status. `past_due` means a charge failed and the subscription is being retried. A freeze or a plan change waiting for renewal is shown on the subscription.

Invoices with their lines, oldest first by `created_at`, or by `updated_at` with `updated_since`. Filter by member, status and subscription. Amounts are in the invoice's own currency; `total` is the gross amount, VAT included.

Feedback, complaints and requests, oldest first by `created_at`, or by `updated_at` with `updated_since`. Filter by `member_id` (a merged member's cases are its survivor's), `status` and `type`. `detail` is included only for a key holding `members:sensitive`. A key limited to venues sees every case, as it sees members.

post.description: Opens a case against a member. A merged member's case goes to whoever they were merged into. Writing `detail` needs `members:sensitive`, as reading it does (403 `insufficient_scope`). Nothing is sent to the member.

get.description: One case of the organisation. `detail` is included only for a key holding `members:sensitive`.

patch.summary: Resolve or dismiss a member case
patch.description: Closes an open case as `resolved` or `dismissed`, with an optional `resolution` note. A case that is not open is 409 `conflict`. Resolving with a `credit` also grants that one-off amount as a loyalty adjustment on the member's oldest loyalty membership, in the organisation's currency: it needs `loyalty:write` as well, and a key with no venue limit (403 otherwise). A member with no loyalty membership can't be credited (400, and the case stays open). A credit on a dismissed case is refused.

get.description: Checks (bills), oldest first by `created_at`, or by `updated_at` with `updated_since`. Filter by `venue_id`, `member_id`, `reservation_id`, `status` and `business_date`: the venue's trading day a check was opened on, from the venue's day cut-off (05:00 by default) to the next day's, on that venue's own clock (a key spanning venues gets each venue's own day). `expand` adds `lines`, `discounts` and/or `payments` to each check; `payments` also needs `payments:read`. A key limited to venues sees only those venues' checks.

parameters.name: reservation_id
parameters.description: The reservation whose booking the check was opened for.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: Comma-separated: lines, discounts, payments. One level only.

get.description: One check. `expand` adds `lines`, `discounts` and/or `payments`; `payments` also needs `payments:read`.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: Comma-separated: lines, discounts, payments. One level only.

get.description: Payments taken on checks, oldest first by `created_at`, or by `updated_at` with `updated_since`. Filter by `check_id`, `venue_id`, `member_id` (the check's member) and `status`. A key limited to venues sees only payments on those venues' checks. The provider's reference and payload are never shown.

post.description: Registers an HTTPS URL to receive events. The endpoint belongs to the calling key. `event_types` are public event types (`member.created`), `<prefix>.*` globs (`event.*`) or `*` for everything the key may see; each one must be a type the key's scopes allow (400 `validation_failed` naming the type). The 201 answer carries the signing `secret`: it is shown here and on `rotate-secret` only, so store it now. A replay of this request with the same `Idempotency-Key` answers the same endpoint with `secret: null`: the secret is never kept for replay, so if it was lost, call `rotate-secret`. A key can have at most 20 endpoints (409 `conflict` past that).

get.description: Only the endpoints the calling key created, oldest first. Another key's endpoints are never listed. The signing secret is not included.
One of the calling key's endpoints. Another key's is 404.

patch.description: Changes `url`, `description`, `event_types` (checked as on create) and `status` (`active` or `paused`). `status: active` resumes a paused endpoint or re-enables one disabled by failures, and restarts its failure clock; deliveries still pending from more than 24 hours before are marked `failed` rather than sent in a burst (read them from the event log, or resend them). A disabled endpoint can't be paused (409).

delete.description: Deletes the endpoint and its delivery log. Nothing more is sent to it.

post.description: Issues a new signing secret, shown only in this answer. Until `previous_expires_at` (24 hours) every delivery carries a signature for both the new and the old secret, so a receiver can switch without dropping events. A replay with the same `Idempotency-Key` answers `secret: null` (the secret is never kept for replay): if it was lost, rotate again. Two rotations at once: one wins, the other is 409 `conflict`.

Queues a `webhook.test` event (`data.object` is `{ endpoint_id }`) to an active endpoint and returns its delivery, which `GET /webhook-endpoints/{id}/deliveries` then follows. A paused or disabled endpoint is 409.

get.description: Newest first. Each delivery is one event to this endpoint with its retries: `attempts`, the last `response_code` and when the next attempt is due.

post.description: Starts a new attempt series for a delivery of one of the key's endpoints: the same event and bytes, attempts back to zero, sent again now.

get.description: The organisation's catalogue events from the last 30 days, oldest first, in the envelope webhooks send. `data.object` is the resource's **current** state, rendered when you read, not when the event happened. Walk it with `after=evt_…` (the last id you have, or `next_cursor`). `types` is a comma list of event types or `<prefix>.*` globs; events whose type the key's scopes don't allow are left out, never an error. A page can hold fewer than `limit` events (and still have more) when events it covered no longer render: a deleted resource, a venue the key can't see, or a module that isn't licensed. Only events at least 10 seconds old are served, so an event committed late can't land behind a cursor you already hold: the log runs that far behind the webhooks.
Bedroom types (sold by the night, and for day use where offered) and meeting rooms (sold by the hour) at a venue, with their rooms.
Price lists at a venue. `audience` says who may book a plan: everyone, members only, or non-members only.
Rooms left per room type and night from `from` up to (not including) `to`, and day-use availability per date. At most 62 nights.
Start times on a date when a minimum-length booking fits, for one meeting room or every room of a meeting room type.

Reservations (tables, event tickets and rooms), oldest first by `created_at` — or by `updated_at` with `updated_since`, for syncing. Filter by venue, kind and status. Kinds the organisation doesn't use are left out.

post.description:
Books a table or a room.

**Table** (`kind: table`): a party at a venue at `starts_at` for `duration_minutes`. With `table_id` the party has that table; without one it has a place at the venue and staff choose the table at seating. A table already booked or held then, one too small for the party, or a venue with no table free answers 409 `table_unavailable`, and nothing is booked.

**Room** (`kind: room`): overnight, day use, or a meeting room by the hour. A member is booked straight away against their card on file (402 `card_required` if they have none). A non-member's booking may be held while they pay: the response is `pending` with `payment.url`, and the room is released at `hold_expires_at` if unpaid. At a venue linked to SynXis, an overnight stay is made there first, and SynXis's answer stands.

A `member_id` of a member merged since books the member they were merged into.

get.description: The free/busy grid for a venue's tables on a date (the venue's own day, midnight to midnight): each bookable table that seats `party_size`, with the times it is taken by a booking, another system's booking, or an event's hold. No slots are worked out; pick a free time and book it, and the booking is checked again.

patch.description: Moves a booked table reservation: its time, length, party size, table or notes. The change is checked as a new booking would be (409 `table_unavailable` when the table or venue can't take it). Rooms and event tickets can't be changed here: 409 `unsupported_for_kind`.

post.description: The party is here: seats them at `table_id`, else at the table they hold, else at the smallest free table that seats them (409 `table_unavailable` when none can). Where the club runs Synapse POS a check is opened on the table. Seating a party already seated changes nothing. Rooms and event tickets: 409 `unsupported_for_kind`.

Cancels a reservation. A table must still be booked (not seated). An event ticket is cancelled without a refund. A room's prepayment is refunded when cancelled before the venue's free-cancellation window, and a payment link still open is closed. Cancelling a cancelled reservation changes nothing.

bad_request.title: Bad request
bad_request.explanation: The request could not be read: malformed JSON, a body on a call that takes none, or a similar problem with its shape.
bad_request.fix: Check the request against the reference for this endpoint. The detail field says what was wrong.

validation_failed.title: Validation failed
validation_failed.explanation: The request was readable but did not match the endpoint's schema. The response carries an errors array, one entry per problem, each with a JSON-pointer-style path and a message.
validation_failed.fix: Fix each field named in errors[].path and send the request again.

invalid_cursor.title: Invalid cursor
invalid_cursor.explanation: The cursor parameter is not one this API issued, or it was changed.
invalid_cursor.fix: Pass next_cursor back exactly as the previous page returned it. To start from the beginning, leave cursor out.

persisted_query_required.title: Persisted query required
persisted_query_required.explanation: Installed apps must send GraphQL queries as automatic persisted queries.
persisted_query_required.fix: Send extensions.persistedQuery { version: 1, sha256Hash } with the query (the SDK does this for you).

idempotency_key_required.title: Idempotency-Key required
idempotency_key_required.explanation: This endpoint creates something or moves money, so it only runs with an Idempotency-Key header.
idempotency_key_required.fix: Send a unique Idempotency-Key header (a UUID is ideal) and reuse it only when retrying the same request.

invalid_idempotency_key.title: Invalid Idempotency-Key
invalid_idempotency_key.explanation: The Idempotency-Key header is longer than 255 characters.
invalid_idempotency_key.fix: Use a shorter key. A UUID is 36 characters.

unauthorized.title: Unauthorized
unauthorized.fix: Send your API key as Authorization: Bearer followed by the key.

invalid_api_key.title: Invalid API key
invalid_api_key.explanation: The Authorization header is missing, is not a Synapse key, or names a key that is unknown, revoked or expired, or belongs to an archived organisation. All of these return the same response on purpose.
invalid_api_key.fix: Check the key in Settings → API keys. If it was revoked or has expired, create a new one.

invalid_token.title: Invalid access token
invalid_token.explanation: The OAuth access token is unknown, expired or revoked, or the app's installation was removed or suspended.
invalid_token.fix: Refresh the token with your refresh token. If refreshing fails, ask the organisation's admin to connect the app again.

forbidden.title: Forbidden
forbidden.explanation: The key is valid but this request is not allowed.
forbidden.fix: Check the detail field. If it is unclear, contact support with the instance value from the response.

insufficient_scope.title: Insufficient scope
insufficient_scope.explanation: The key does not carry every scope this endpoint needs. The response lists the scopes the call needs in required and the ones the key lacks in missing.
insufficient_scope.fix: Create a key with the missing scopes in Settings → API keys. Keys cannot be edited, so replace the old one.

product_not_licensed.title: Product not licensed
product_not_licensed.explanation: The endpoint belongs to a Synapse product the organisation does not subscribe to.
product_not_licensed.fix: Ask the venue to enable the product, or stop calling this endpoint for that organisation.

module_not_licensed.title: Module not licensed
module_not_licensed.explanation: The endpoint belongs to a module that is not enabled for the organisation.
module_not_licensed.fix: Ask the venue to enable the module, or stop calling this endpoint for that organisation.

card_required.title: Card required
card_required.explanation: The venue only takes room bookings from members who have a card on file, and this member has none (or only an expired one, or one with a different payment provider).
card_required.fix: Ask the member to add a card with the club, then book again with a new Idempotency-Key (a retry with the same key replays this answer for 24 hours). Non-members don't need one: they get a payment link instead.

org_locked.title: Organisation locked
org_locked.explanation: The organisation's Synapse subscription has ended and its account is locked. Every key it issued is refused until it restarts its subscription; nothing about the key itself is wrong.
org_locked.fix: Ask the venue to restart its subscription. Keep the key: it works again, unchanged, as soon as the venue does.

not_found.title: Not found
not_found.explanation: No record with that ID exists in the key's organisation. An ID with the wrong prefix, such as a reservation ID passed where a member ID is expected, is also not found.
not_found.fix: Check the ID and its prefix. IDs from another organisation are never visible.

route_not_found.title: Route not found
route_not_found.explanation: No endpoint exists at this method and path.
route_not_found.fix: Check the path against the reference. Every path starts with /public/v1/.

method_not_allowed.title: Method not allowed
method_not_allowed.explanation: The path exists but does not accept this HTTP method.
method_not_allowed.fix: Use the method shown for this path in the reference.

conflict.title: Conflict
conflict.explanation: The request conflicts with the current state of the record.
conflict.fix: Fetch the record again, then decide whether to retry.

venue_not_found.title: Venue not found
venue_not_found.explanation: The venue_id names no venue that this key can use: it does not exist in the organisation, or the key is limited to other venues.
venue_not_found.fix: Use a venue ID from GET /venues, and one the key covers.

invalid_transition.title: Invalid transition
invalid_transition.explanation: An applicant cannot move from its current status to the one asked for, or cannot be converted yet because it is not approved.
invalid_transition.fix: Fetch the applicant, check its status, and move it along the review pipeline one allowed step at a time.

applicant_converted.title: Applicant already converted
applicant_converted.explanation: The applicant has become a member, so it can no longer be edited or decided.
applicant_converted.fix: Use converted_member_id to find the member and change the member instead.

proposers_unconfirmed.title: Proposers unconfirmed
proposers_unconfirmed.explanation: Approving would pass over proposers who have not all confirmed. The response lists them in proposers, each with a name and status.
proposers_unconfirmed.fix: Wait for the proposers to confirm, or send the decision again with override_proposers set to true to approve anyway.

member_merged.title: Member merged
member_merged.explanation: This member was merged into another and can no longer be changed. A GET on it still answers, with status merged and merged_into naming the member that took its place.
member_merged.fix: Make the change on the member in merged_into.

merge_conflict.title: Merge not possible
merge_conflict.explanation: The two members can't be merged: they are the same member, or one of them has already been merged.
merge_conflict.fix: Check both ids. To merge into a member that was itself merged, use the member in its merged_into.

merge_blocked.title: Merge blocked by billing
merge_blocked.explanation: The member being merged away still has live billing: a subscription, an unpaid invoice, an account balance, a direct debit, a scheduled first payment or a saved card. The blockers array names each one. Nothing was changed.
merge_blocked.fix: Ask the club to settle or move that billing in Synapse, then merge again.

unsupported_for_kind.title: Not for this kind of reservation
unsupported_for_kind.explanation: This action doesn't apply to this reservation's kind: a room stay can't be seated, and a ticket's time and party are the event's.
unsupported_for_kind.fix: Check the reservation's kind. Change an event ticket through /tickets, and a room stay by cancelling and booking again.

table_unavailable.title: Table unavailable
table_unavailable.explanation: The table is already booked or held at that time, it can't take the party, or no table at the venue is free.
table_unavailable.fix: Ask GET /reservations/availability for a free table and time, then book again.

sold_out.title: Sold out
sold_out.explanation: The event, or the ticket tier asked for, has no places left, or its sales window is closed.
sold_out.fix: Offer a different tier or event. Nothing was reserved.

admission_refused.title: Admission refused
admission_refused.explanation: The venue's door rules refused this check-in: the event is at its capacity limit, the person is flagged not to be admitted, or the ticket isn't valid for entry. The detail says which. Only staff at the door can override.
admission_refused.fix: Send the guest to the door staff.

already_checked_in.title: Already checked in
already_checked_in.explanation: Everyone on this ticket has already checked in.
already_checked_in.fix: Nothing to do. GET the ticket to see when.

already_collected.title: Already collected
already_collected.explanation: This cloakroom ticket was already collected.
already_collected.fix: Nothing to do. GET the ticket to see its status.

idempotency_in_flight.title: Request in progress
idempotency_in_flight.explanation: A request with the same Idempotency-Key is still running.
idempotency_in_flight.fix: Wait a moment and retry with the same key. You will get the original response once it finishes.

payload_too_large.title: Payload too large
payload_too_large.explanation: The request body is larger than the API accepts.
payload_too_large.fix: Send a smaller body. Split bulk work into several requests.

unsupported_media_type.title: Unsupported media type
unsupported_media_type.explanation: The Content-Type header is not one this endpoint reads.

unprocessable.title: Unprocessable
unprocessable.explanation: The request was valid but could not be carried out.
unprocessable.fix: Read the detail field for the reason.

idempotency_key_reused.title: Idempotency-Key reused
idempotency_key_reused.explanation: This Idempotency-Key was already used in the last 24 hours with a different method, path or body.
idempotency_key_reused.fix: Use a new key for a new request. Reuse a key only to retry exactly the same request.

rate_limited.title: Rate limit exceeded
rate_limited.explanation: The key has used its request budget: a burst of 50, refilled at 1,000 an hour. The Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.
rate_limited.fix: Wait for Retry-After seconds, then retry. Watch RateLimit-Remaining to slow down before you hit the limit.

too_many_failed_attempts.title: Too many failed attempts
too_many_failed_attempts.explanation: After 30 failed authentication attempts in a minute from one address, requests are refused until the minute is up, even with a valid key.
too_many_failed_attempts.fix: Fix the key your client sends, then wait for Retry-After seconds.

venue_not_ready.title: Venue not ready for online booking
venue_not_ready.explanation: The venue hasn't finished setting up what this booking needs, such as a payment provider to take guests' payments. Retrying won't help until the venue does.
venue_not_ready.fix: Ask the venue to finish its payment set-up. Members with a card on file can still be booked.

unavailable.title: Temporarily unavailable
unavailable.explanation: Something the request depends on can't be reached right now, such as the venue's payment provider or its hotel reservation system. Nothing was booked.
unavailable.fix: Try again in a moment with a new Idempotency-Key. If it keeps happening, contact the venue.

internal_error.title: Internal error
internal_error.explanation: Something went wrong on our side. The request may or may not have taken effect.
internal_error.fix: Retry with the same Idempotency-Key if the call takes one. If it keeps happening, contact support with the instance value.
